findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations in the cron run
findings.body:
The loop awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder inside a single try/catch. If one request throws (invalid batch id, rate limit, or the 100 pending-cancellation cap), the loop stops. Every remaining reminder in that run is left uncancelled.

The delete operations already collected are lazy Prisma promises that only run at `Promise.all`, which is never reached. So even reminders that were cancelled successfully stay in the DB. The failing reminder is likely to break subsequent runs the same way until its scheduledDate passes, and the affected emails go out.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own try/catch and delete each row right after its cancel succeeds.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation can miss reminders that are close to their send time
findings.body:
Cancellation only marks `cancelled: true`. The real SendGrid cancel waits for the next cron run, which happens every 15 minutes.

Suppose a booking is cancelled or rescheduled shortly before a reminder's send time, for example right after a cron tick and less than about 15–25 minutes before sendAt. The next cron run may come too late, either after the send or inside SendGrid's minimum lead time for cancelling a scheduled send. The email for the cancelled booking is still delivered, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Fix: cancel immediately when scheduledDate is within the cron window (for example under 1h15m away), and defer only reminders further in the future.

findings.title: Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation and leaves stale rows
findings.body:
When a booking is rescheduled, its reminders are cancelled with `immediateDelete = true`. That calls the SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel right away, and those pending cancellations count against the 100-cancellation cap. Reschedules are frequent, so this brings back the failure mode the PR describes.

In the immediate branch, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` also neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, so stale `scheduled: true` rows remain for the old booking.

The same reminders may already have been marked cancelled by `requestReschedule`, in which case they are cancelled twice. Use the deferred `cancelled` flag here as well.

findings.title: immediateDelete branch never removes the DB record
findings.body:
When `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns. It never deletes or flags the WorkflowReminder row.

For workflow or step deletion, the row is removed later by cascade. Other callers, such as the reschedule path in handleNewBooking, are left with a row that still says `scheduled: true` and has no `cancelled` flag. That row is inconsistent with reality and is only cleaned up after its scheduledDate passes.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget
findings.body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are called inside `forEach` without being awaited. The handler can return before the `cancelled` flag update or the Twilio cancel and DB delete finish.

In serverless deployments, work still pending after the response may be dropped. A dropped flag update means the cron never cancels the email. Previously the DB deletes were at least awaited through `Promise.all`, and the same regression applies in bookings.tsx `requestReschedule` and in workflows.tsx.

Fix: collect the promises and await them.
